changes.text: 先看韩信这支部队的处境。据《淮阴侯列传》所记，李左车对成安君陈述汉军的来路：韩信涉西河、虏魏王、禽夏说，又在阏与打过硬仗，如今加上张耳，议欲下赵，这是乘胜而离国远斗，「其鋒不可當」。但同一段里他又算了另一笔账：千里运粮，士有饥色，砍了柴再做饭，部队不能常饱；井陉这条路车不能并轨、骑兵不能成列，行军数百里，粮食一定落在后面。优势和软肋是同一支军队的两面。

Start with what Han Xin's army was up against. In the "Account of the Marquis of Huaiyin," one chapter of Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian, Li Zuoche — the Lord of Guangwu — traces the Han army's road to Zhao: Han Xin crossed the Western River, captured the King of Wei, took Xia Yue alive, and fought a bloody battle at Yuyu; with Zhang Er now beside him he means to bring down Zhao. This is an army riding its victories far from home, and its edge, in his words, cannot be withstood. But Li Zuoche keeps a second ledger in the same breath: grain hauled a thousand li leaves soldiers with hunger on their faces; you cut firewood before you can cook, and no army stays fed. On the Jingxing road two carts cannot run abreast and cavalry cannot form a column; after several hundred li, the supplies must be somewhere behind. Strength and frailty were two faces of one army.
李左车给出的方案因此很具体：请拨奇兵三万人，抄小路断掉汉军辎重；主力深沟高垒，坚守不出战。汉军向前无仗可打、后退无路可走，后路被断、野外无处征粮，他估计不至十日，「兩將之頭可致於戲下」。他最后还留了一句警告：否则，「必爲二子所禽矣」——必定会被这两个人擒住。

His proposal followed from that. He asked to be lent a surprise force of thirty thousand to cut the Han baggage train by the side roads, while the main body held behind deep ditches and high walls and refused battle. Ahead the Han would have no one to fight; behind them no way back; with their rear cut and nothing to forage in the open country, he reckoned that in less than ten days the heads of the two generals could be delivered to the commander's tent. He closed with a warning: otherwise, he said, you will surely be taken by those two.
赵国这边的主帅成安君陈馀，本传在记他拒计时对他有这样一句定性：「儒者也，常稱義兵不用詐謀奇計」。他拒绝的理由也被记了下来，可以分成三层：一是算术，兵法说十倍可以围、倍数可以战，韩信号称数万、其实不过数千，千里奔袭已经疲惫到极点；二是往后，如果这样还避而不击，以后来了更强的敌人又怎么应付；三是名声，那样「則諸侯謂吾怯，而輕來伐我」。他没有采纳广武君的计策。

Chen Yu, the Lord of Cheng'an and Zhao's commander-in-chief, is characterized in this biography, at the point where he refuses the plan, as a Confucian who always maintained that a righteous army does not use deceit and cunning schemes. His grounds for refusing are recorded too, and they fall into three layers. One is arithmetic: the manual says ten-to-one besieges, two-to-one fights; Han Xin claims tens of thousands but has no more than a few thousand, and a thousand-li raid has worn them to the bone. The second looks ahead: if he avoided battle like this, how would he meet a stronger enemy that came later? The third is reputation: in his words roughly, the lords would then think him cowardly and come lightly to attack him. He did not take the Guangwu Jun's advice.
埋伏的二千轻骑等的就是这一刻：赵营空了，他们驰入营垒，拔掉赵旗，插上二千面汉军红旗。赵军在前面不能取胜、又抓不到韩信，想回营时，看到的是「壁皆漢赤幟」，大惊，以为汉军已经把赵王和将领都拿下了，队伍顿时乱了，将领杀人弹压也止不住。汉军前后夹击，大破赵军，斩成安君于泜水上，擒赵王歇。

The ambush had been waiting for exactly that. With the Zhao camp emptied, the two thousand riders swept in, pulled down the Zhao banners and raised two thousand red ones of Han. Beaten in front and unable to catch Han Xin, the Zhao troops turned for their camp and found the walls all hung with Han's red banners. Greatly alarmed, they were sure the Han had already taken the king of Zhao and his generals. The army dissolved; commanders cut men down to hold the line and could not. The Han struck from both sides, routed the Zhao army, killed the Lord of Cheng'an on the banks of the Zhi, and took King Xie alive.
庆功时诸将问了一个问题：兵法说布阵要右背山陵、前左水泽，将军却令我们背水列阵，还说破赵后会食，我们本来不服气，可居然胜了，这是什么术？韩信的回答是：这也在兵法里，只是诸位没细看，兵法不是说「陷之死地而後生，置之亡地而後存」吗？他说自己统带的不是长期抚循的旧部，是所谓「驅市人而戰之」，形势上非得把他们放进死地，让人人为自己的性命而战；若给他们留了生路，就全都跑了，还怎么用。诸将服气。

At the celebration the generals asked a question. The manual says to keep hills at the right rear and water at the left front; you ordered us to form up with our backs to the water, and said we would eat after Zhao was broken. We were not convinced — yet we won. What art is this? Han Xin's answer: it is in the manual; you simply failed to see it there. Does it not say that men thrown onto death ground will live, and men placed where destruction is certain will survive? The men I have are not old followers I have cared for over the years; this is what is called driving men of the marketplace to fight. The situation demanded putting them on death ground, so that every man fought for his own life; give them ground to live in and they would all run, and then what use would they be? The generals conceded the point.

原文又记李左车说：「智者千慮，必有一失；愚者千慮，必有一得」，所以有句话说，狂夫之言，圣人也从中择取。这句话不是结局，而是献计前的铺垫：他接着说担心自己的计未必足用，但愿效愚忠，随即举成安君为例——有百战百胜之计，却「一旦而失之」，军败身死；然后献上自己的方案：按兵休整、镇抚赵地，再派辩士送信到燕国，向燕显示己方所长，并说「兵固有先聲而後實者」。韩信说「善」，「從其策」，派使者去燕，燕国「從風而靡」。一种解读是：他刚说的智者之失，紧接着就落在成安君身上；而韩信对出计者的对待，最后不只是礼遇，而是实际采用了他的计。

The text also records Li Zuoche saying that the wise man, in a thousand considerations, must have one failure, and the fool, in a thousand considerations, must have one success — hence the saying, the sage still picks through a madman's words. This was not the end but the preface to a plan. He went on to say he feared his plan might not be adequate but wished to offer his humble loyalty, and pointed to the Lord of Cheng'an, who had a plan that could win a hundred battles out of a hundred and lost it at a stroke, his army beaten and himself killed. Then he laid out his own proposal: rest the troops, settle Zhao, and send a persuader with a letter to Yan displaying Han's strengths, since in war there are times when reputation comes first and substance after. Han Xin said, Good, followed his plan, and sent an envoy to Yan; Yan bent like grass before the wind. One reading: the failure of the wise man he had just spoken of falls at once on the Lord of Cheng'an; and Han Xin's treatment of the adviser ended not merely in courtesy but in actually adopting his plan.

把原文所记陈馀拒绝的理由拆开看，会发现它们不是一类东西。「兵號數萬，其實不過數千」「千里而襲我，亦已罷極」是对敌情的判断，可以争论；「後有大者，何以加之」既不完全是对眼前汉军的判断，也不完全是形象问题，而是对以后局面的预想；“避而不击，诸侯就会说我怯懦”则不是对汉军的判断，是对自身形象的判断。此外，史家在记这些理由之前，先交代了他平日的立场：「常稱義兵不用詐謀奇計」。这是司马迁对他一贯说法的描述，不是他这一次拒绝时给出的理由；而且它不是判断，是一条规矩。一种解释是：这条规矩与李左车的奇兵之计正好相冲，二者或有关联，但原文并没有把它记为这次拒绝的理由。作者推断，这也是为什么原文要给陈馀加上「儒者也」这个身份标签——史家记的是立场，不只是失策。

Split apart the reasons the text records for Chen Yu's refusal and they are not the same kind of thing. Claims tens of thousands, really no more than a few thousand; a thousand-li raid has worn them to the bone — those are readings of the enemy, contestable in principle. If we avoid battle now, how will we meet a stronger enemy later is neither wholly a reading of the Han army in front of him nor wholly a matter of image; it is a projection about situations to come. Refuse battle and the lords will think me cowardly is not a reading of the Han army at all; it is a reading of his own image. Before recording those reasons, the historian also sets out his habitual stance: he always maintained that a righteous army does not use deceit and cunning schemes. That is Sima Qian's description of what Chen Yu habitually said, not a reason he gave for this refusal; and it is not a judgment at all but a rule. One explanation: that rule runs directly against Li Zuoche's surprise-force plan, and the two may be connected, but the text does not record it as a ground for this refusal. The author's inference is that this is why the text labels Chen Yu a Confucian: the historian is recording a stance, not merely a mistake.
第二个细节值得盯住：韩信并非胸有成竹地长驱直入，他是「使人閒視，知其不用」之后才敢进兵的。换句话说，那条没被采纳的计，是他的作战前提之一；两千轻骑的得手取决于赵军倾巢逐利，万人背水是另一重安排，而作者推断，赵军倾巢逐利这个条件只在李左车之计被弃后才成立。一种解释是，情报在这场胜负里的分量不低于阵法：韩信先确认了对手不会听对的意见，然后才把自己放进战场。

Second detail worth holding onto: Han Xin did not march in on confidence. He advanced only after sending men to spy on the Zhao side and learning the plan had not been used. The rejected proposal was, in other words, one of the premises of his battle. The two thousand riders' success depended on the Zhao army emptying its camp to chase; the ten thousand men with the river at their backs were a separate arrangement. The author's inference is that this condition held only because Li Zuoche's plan had been shelved. One explanation: intelligence carried as much weight in this victory as formation. Han Xin first confirmed that his opponent would not listen to sound advice, then placed himself on the field.
还有一个容易被忽略的不对称。战后诸将问的是“为什么背水”，也就是问赢家的招数妙在哪里；在诸将战后问答这一段里，没有人问“那条计当初为什么没被采纳”。作者推断，复盘天然聚光在胜者的技巧上，因为技巧可学；而一次否决看上去毫无技术含量，也不产生任何战果。可作者认为，这场仗里决定性的动作恰恰发生在开战之前——一次拒绝，和一次对拒绝的探知。

There is also an easy-to-miss asymmetry. After the battle the generals asked why the backs-to-the-water formation — a question about what made the winner's move clever. In the generals' post-battle exchange as recorded, no one asks why that plan had not been adopted before the fighting. The author's inference: after-action review naturally spotlights the winner's technique, because technique can be learned, while a veto looks like it takes no skill and yields no result. Yet in the author's view, the decisive acts in this battle happened before the first blow fell — a refusal, and the discovery of that refusal.

韩信本人把结论说得比谁都直白：他借百里奚的例子说，关键在「用與不用，聽與不聽也」，并说若成安君听足下计，我已经被擒。需要说清楚的是，这是韩信自己事后的说法，不是可以检验的事实；战场没有第二次。作者提出的替代情形是：如果陈馀采纳李左车之计、坚壁不出并断其辎重，韩信会怎么改，史书没有记载，任何人都只能推测。可以确认的是：韩信的部署以赵军会追出来为条件；至于赵军追出来与那条计被否决之间的关系有多直接，是作者的推断。

Han Xin put the conclusion more bluntly than anyone: speaking of Baili Xi, he said it turned on whether a man is used or not, heeded or not, and that had the Lord of Cheng'an listened to you, I would be the captive. To be clear, that is Han Xin's own account after the event, not a fact anyone can check; battles are not run twice. The alternative the author raises: had Chen Yu adopted the plan, held his walls and cut the supplies, what Han Xin would have done instead is unrecorded and can only be guessed at. What can be established is that his deployment depended on the Zhao army coming out to chase; how directly that depended on the plan's rejection is the author's inference.
本文所有事实都来自司马迁《史记·淮阴侯列传》一篇，本文没有使用第二个史源作交叉验证。也就是说，李左车的算粮、陈馀的理由、诸将的疑问、李左车的谦辞，都出自同一作者的记述；对话是史书的记述，未必是现场的逐字原话，本文使用其中原句处，只取原文中确有的文字。

Every fact here comes from one text, Sima Qian's "Account of the Marquis of Huaiyin"; this piece uses no second source to cross-check against. Li Zuoche's supply arithmetic, Chen Yu's reasons, the generals' questions, Li Zuoche's modesty — all of it is a single author's record. The speeches are the historian's account and need not be verbatim transcripts; where this piece uses the original wording, it takes only phrasing actually present in the text.
另一种做法（作者提出）：先不争论方案本身，先换取信息——正如韩信「使人閒視」，先确认对方会不会真的照那条路走，再决定自己进退。

Another approach, proposed by the author: set the merits of the proposal aside first and buy information instead — as Han Xin sent men to spy on the Zhao camp, confirm whether the other side will actually take that route before deciding your own advance or retreat.

dispositions.rationale: 英文去掉引号，改为“its edge, in his words, cannot be withstood”的转述，不再冒充原文直引；中文「其鋒不可當」为逐字原文，保持不变。
英文把“thirty thousand picked troops”改为“a surprise force of thirty thousand”，与中文“奇兵”和 analysis.0 的 surprise-force 一致。

evidence.quote: 願足下假臣奇兵三萬人

dispositions.rationale: 删去“只有一句/one line”的全称断言，中文改为“本传在记他拒计时对他有这样一句定性”，英文同步改写。

evidence.quote: 成安君，儒者也，常稱義兵不用詐謀奇計

dispositions.rationale: 把“两层”改为三层，补上原文记载的“以后来了更强的敌人又怎么应付”一条，中英同步。

evidence.quote: 今如此避而不擊，後有大者，何以加之！

dispositions.rationale: 英文删去原文没有的限定语“at such odds”，改为“avoided battle like this”。
英文去掉引号，改为转述：found the walls all hung with Han's red banners; greatly alarmed。
英文的兵法句和“驱市人而战之”都改为不加引号的转述；中文的逐字引语不变。

evidence.quote: 陷之死地而後生，置之亡地而後存

dispositions.rationale: 补写李左车在谦辞后举成安君“一旦而失之”为例，随后献计（按兵休整、镇抚赵地、遣辩士致书于燕、先声后实）；韩信称善并“從其策”，燕国“從風而靡”。原“任何人都可能出错”的解读改为：智者之失落在成安君身上，韩信最终实际采纳了他的计。ev 增加 J-E11，中英同步。

evidence.quote: 顧恐臣計未必足用，願效愚忠
夫成安君有百戰百勝之計，一旦而失之
韓信曰：『善。』從其策，發使使燕，燕從風而靡

dispositions.rationale: 把「後有大者，何以加之」列入拆分，说明它既不完全是对眼前汉军的判断，也不完全是形象问题，而是对以后局面的预想，使归类覆盖原文全部理由；中英同步。
英文去掉引号，改为转述：sending men to spy on the Zhao side and learning the plan had not been used。

evidence.quote: 韓信使人閒視，知其不用

dispositions.rationale: 把对全篇的缺失断言收窄为“在诸将战后问答这一段里，没有人问那条计为何被否”，英文同步。
英文去掉引号，改为“whether a man is used or not, heeded or not”的转述，并注明这是借百里奚而言；中文同步补上“他借百里奚的例子说”。
把“没有第二个独立史源”的存在性断言改为“本文没有使用第二个史源作交叉验证”，英文同步。
英文去掉引号，改为 as Han Xin sent men to spy on the Zhao camp；中文的古文引语顺带由“”改为「」，以符合引语规范。
